stages.title: Design
objectives: Plan one CubeSat to watch Sarawak's rainforest.
Make department decisions with the four crew specialists.
Complete Rocket Fit, One Orbit, Pass Planner and Payload Bay.
Keep budget, mass and 24-month readiness within their limits.
summary: Define > Design > Review > Launch > Operate > Report.
Fit a forest imager; cover Sarawak; return at least 70% of data.
Design for two years in orbit, within 2.5 M and the spacecraft mass limit.
Be ready within 24 months. Nadia plans, Daniel builds, Mei Ling connects, Aina studies.
Every choice costs something. Work together; mistakes teach us.
Maps and spacecraft graphics are mission schematics, not live observations.
hazards: Science needs power, mass and downlink time; leave room for all three.
Cloud cover can reduce useful forest images.
Opening or replaying this briefing does not change your saved design.

segments.speaker: hamdan
segments.text: Our forests are our future. A CubeSat. Shoebox size. It will watch our forests from space.

segments.speaker: hamdan
segments.text: We have two years and a small budget. We need a team. Not astronauts. Planners. Engineers. You.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Welcome. Two years. 2.5 million. One forest-watching CubeSat for Sarawak. Let's make each choice count.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Talk to each other. All green before launch. Every choice costs something. And mistakes teach us.

segments.speaker: jabu
segments.text: Daniel, check mass, power and battery together. A good spacecraft survives the nights as well as the days.

segments.speaker: ling
segments.text: Mei Ling, give the data a way home. Our target is at least 70% returned. Plan your ground-station passes.

segments.speaker: siti
segments.text: Aina, bring a forest imager. We need useful views of Sarawak, with a plan for clouds. No pressure. Only science.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Nadia, keep us within 2.5 M and 24 months. Meet the crew, make department choices, then solve the four Core puzzles.

stages.title: Review & Launch
objectives: Review your saved design and its live requirement checks.
Resolve power, mass, orbit, budget and downlink conflicts.
Choose Go or Hold, then complete the eight ordered launch checks.
Authorize the actual launch only at its gameplay checkpoint.
summary: Now it all has to fit together. No wrong answer. Just a different mission.
Check power versus science, mass versus communications, and orbit versus imaging needs.
Match data production to downlink capacity; protect budget and schedule margins.
Check in order: Power > Battery > Antenna > Instruments > Mass > Orbit > Budget > Schedule.
Go commits the review decision; Hold gives you a route to revise.
Accepting this briefing starts review. It does not ignite a rocket or bypass the checklist.
hazards: A red requirement needs revision before an authorized launch.
An imager can produce more data than your radio can return.
Launch can fail. Keep the lesson and begin a fresh attempt without blame.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Now it all has to fit together. Your saved design is on the board. Let's check what each choice means for the others.

segments.speaker: jabu
segments.text: Power versus science. Mass versus communications. Check the battery too; daylight is only half our story.

segments.speaker: siti
segments.text: Orbit changes what we can image, and how long we stay up. Keep Sarawak and our two-year life in view.

segments.speaker: ling
segments.text: Data made is not data returned. Check downlink capacity against the imager and protect that 70% target.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: No wrong answer. Just a different mission. Keep budget and schedule in range, then choose Go or Hold.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Eight checks: Power, Battery, Antenna, Instruments, Mass, Orbit, Budget, Schedule. In that order.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Accept takes you to review. Launch waits for its real checkpoint. If we need to revise, better here than in orbit.

stages.title: Operations & Report
objectives: Respond to seven quarterly events, Q2 through Q8.
Protect power, orbital life and useful data return.
Review actual results, requirement checks and one next-attempt lesson.
summary: Signal acquisition and first light over Sarawak begin operations; this stage does not launch another satellite.
Q2 heavy cloud: Aina adjusts science. Q3 station outage: Mei Ling protects communications.
Q4 rain at the dish: Mei Ling handles Rain Fade. Q5 long eclipse: Daniel triages power.
Q6 instrument glitch: Aina follows the reset sequence. Q7 debris warning: Daniel plays Debris Dodge.
Q8 battery heating: Daniel manages cooling and loads.
Final reports use saved decisions, puzzle tiers, requirement numbers and the mission outcome.
Forest previews are labelled illustrations or simulations, not live satellite imagery.
hazards: Cloud and rain can cut useful science and downlink capacity.
Long eclipses and battery heating threaten available power.
Debris risk depends on your actual design and response.
Keep the spacecraft alive while returning useful forest data.

segments.speaker: ling
segments.text: Signal acquired. First light over Sarawak. Our CubeSat is already up; now we keep it alive and bring useful data home.

segments.speaker: siti
segments.text: Q2: heavy cloud. Aina, adjust the imaging plan. Clear views matter more than a full tank of cloudy pictures.

segments.speaker: ling
segments.text: Q3: station outage. Mei Ling, protect the data and choose how to recover our ground link.

segments.speaker: ling
segments.text: Q4: rain at the dish. Mei Ling, Rain Fade is yours. Watch the weather and keep the downlink working.

segments.speaker: jabu
segments.text: Q5: a long eclipse. Daniel, triage the loads and protect the battery. The night does not take requests.

segments.speaker: siti
segments.text: Q6: instrument glitch. Aina, follow the reset sequence so we can return to useful forest imaging.

segments.speaker: jabu
segments.text: Q7: debris warning. Daniel, prepare for Debris Dodge. Check our options and steer early if the design allows it.

segments.speaker: aisyah
segments.text: Q8: battery heating. Daniel, manage cooling and loads. Then we'll review what flew, what worked and what we learned.

acknowledgments.speaker: aisyah
acknowledgments.text: Authorized. Meet the crew at the Mess Hall table. Your forest-watch design starts together.

acknowledgments.speaker: aisyah
acknowledgments.text: Authorized for review. Bring your saved design to the crew. Go or Hold and the launch checks still come next.

acknowledgments.speaker: ling
acknowledgments.text: Operations link ready. Our CubeSat is already in orbit. The crew will help you bring its data home.
